=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: Lines 835-852, inside _evaluate_fp_state, the two print blocks that emit the FINGERPRINT_PARTIAL_REMOVAL_FALSE_POSITIVE_V1 markers and the human-readable warning
  Problem: Both print calls use the default stdout without file=sys.stderr. The _evaluate_fp_state function is called from list_violated_files (line ~940), which explicitly documents its stdout contract as "file paths ONLY" (line 931). When the verifier runs in --list-violated-files mode and encounters a partial-removal false positive, the ::warning:: lines and human-readable diagnostics are emitted to stdout alongside the resolved file-path list.
  Why it fails at runtime: The --list-violated-files mode feeds its stdout into the resolver's working-set expansion in scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh. These injected diagnostic lines would be parsed as file paths by the resolver, either causing malformed path expansion or injecting garbage entries that the resolver cannot resolve. The existing diagnostic prints elsewhere in the same file (line 176, line 734) already use file=sys.stderr, establishing the convention this code should follow.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: Line 347, f"--grep=#{pr_str}\\b" inside _find_pr_merge_commit_for_path
  Problem: The \b word-boundary escape in the --grep extended-regex (-E) pattern is a glibc extension. POSIX extended regular expressions do not define \b as a word boundary; on non-glibc regex implementations (BSD, macOS), \b is treated as a literal backspace character (0x08). Since commit messages do not contain literal backspace characters, the git log --grep pre-filter returns zero results on those platforms, and _find_pr_merge_commit_for_path returns None.
  Why it fails at runtime: On CI (Ubuntu/glibc runners) the behavior is correct. On non-glibc developer workstations, the verifier-side partial-removal defense is effectively disabled — _is_must_not_contain_partial_removal_false_positive returns None, and the original violation surfaces. The defense is documented as fail-open (returning None is safe), so this is not a correctness regression at runtime. It is a portability gap that silently reduces defense coverage on non-glibc platforms. The actual match logic (subject.rstrip().endswith(merge_suffix) in Python) is correct and does not depend on the grep pre-filter.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Test plan — [x] tests/test_verify_integration_fingerprints_partial_removal.py (new, 9 tests): Helper returns merge commit SHA when the pattern still appears... End-to-end main() exits 0 with the marker... End-to-end main() STILL exits 1... Capture heredoc drops the must_not_contain entry... Capture heredoc preserves the must_not_contain entry... Capture heredoc fails open when FINGERPRINT_POST_MERGE_REF is empty." The PR description also states "Existing test_capture_intent_fingerprints_* (9 tests in tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py) still pass..." and "bash -n scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh clean; verify_integration_fingerprints.py imports cleanly."
  Expected change site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py (sub-runner pattern matching test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline_regressions at line 7210), or .github/workflows/ci.yml / .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml / .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml (explicit python3 tests/... allowlists)
  Evidence of absence: The string "test_verify_integration_fingerprints_partial_removal" does not appear in any file under .github/workflows/ or tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py. The existing pattern for wiring standalone verifier test suites into CI is test_verify_integration_fingerprints_baseline_regressions (line 7210 of test_orchestrate_poll_process.py), which imports and runs the baseline suite via importlib. No equivalent sub-runner exists for the partial-removal suite. Without this wiring, the 10 test functions in the new 566-line file never execute in CI — a future change that breaks the partial-removal defense would not be caught by any automated test.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: 829-845
  Problem: The `FINGERPRINT_PARTIAL_REMOVAL_FALSE_POSITIVE_V1` diagnostic prints go to stdout instead of stderr. The script has a `--list-violated-files` mode where stdout is contractually required to contain only file paths. These warnings will pollute the output and can break downstream tools that consume the path list.
  Why it fails at runtime: When the verifier runs in list-violated-files mode, the warning messages are interleaved with file paths, causing parsers to receive malformed output.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: agents.md
  Line or code reference: 254-255
  Problem: The documentation states "the partial-removal guard emits `FINGERPRINT_PARTIAL_REMOVAL_FALSE_POSITIVE_V1`" but this misattributes the marker emission. The marker is actually emitted by the verifier in `_evaluate_fp_state` (lines 829-845), not by the capture-side guard. The capture-side only filters entries - it does not emit markers.
  Why it fails at runtime: Operator-facing documentation is inaccurate and can mislead debugging when the marker appears in logs.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py
  Line or code reference: 347 (git log --grep pattern)
  Problem: The regex pattern `f"--grep=#{pr_str}\\b"` with `-E` flag uses `\b` as a word boundary, which is a glibc extension and not portable in POSIX extended regular expressions. On non-glibc systems, this will fail to match squash-merge commit subjects.
  Why it fails at runtime: On non-glibc platforms (some BSDs, macOS in certain configurations), `_find_pr_merge_commit_for_path` returns None, the verifier-side defense fails open, and partial-removal false positives are not detected.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
